<med>EPDS</med>

Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling now that your baby has arrived. We’ll use a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS. It’s simply 10 questions about your mood, thoughts, and well-being over the past week. There are no right or wrong answers, and everything you share stays between us. My goal is to understand how you’re coping so we can make sure you get the support you deserve. When you’re ready, we can start with the first question.

Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I can laugh sometimes, but honestly, it feels like a lot of effort. My sister sent me a funny video yesterday and I managed a little chuckle, but it faded pretty quickly. Most of the time I just feel too tired or stressed to find things funny.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
No… not really. I might force a little smile if someone shows me something funny, but mostly I feel too heavy inside to laugh.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much. I used to get excited about little things—like grabbing coffee with friends or even just a quiet shower—but lately I barely think about them. When I do imagine doing something I used to enjoy, it feels flat, like “what’s the point?” I still go through the motions, but the happy buzz I used to feel isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m not feeding him right or I’m missing some cue. Yesterday he cried for almost an hour and I kept replaying every little thing I did, convinced it was my fault. Even when my partner says the baby’s just fussy, I still feel like I must be failing somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much all the time. Even when everything looks fine—the baby’s breathing fine, he just ate, he’s warm—I still catch myself staring at the monitor or hovering over the crib to make sure he’s okay. My heart races over things I know are small, like whether the bottle temperature was exactly right or if I burped him long enough. I can’t seem to turn the worry off, even when there’s no real reason.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes—sometimes it hits me out of nowhere. I’ll be folding laundry and suddenly my chest gets tight, my heart’s racing, and I feel like something awful is about to happen. I know there’s no real danger, but in that moment it’s like I need to run or hide. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days. Between feedings, diapers, laundry, and trying to grab a shower, it feels like I’m drowning in small tasks. Some mornings I just lie there staring at the ceiling, wondering how I’ll get through the next hour, let alone the whole day. I manage, but it’s like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I’ll lie down exhausted, but my mind keeps circling—worrying I forgot something, replaying every cry, imagining worst-case scenarios. Some nights I finally drift off, then jolt awake sure I heard the baby when he’s actually still asleep. It’s like I can’t turn the “mom switch” off long enough to rest.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes, that’s most days. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling that just sits on me. I’ll look at my beautiful baby and feel like I *should* be happy, but instead there’s this constant ache. Some afternoons I just sit on the couch and cry for no clear reason, then feel guilty for wasting time. It’s like the sadness is always humming in the background.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it happens. A few times a week I’ll just start crying—sometimes when I’m nursing, sometimes when I’m folding onesies. It feels like the tears come out of nowhere, but at the same time it’s everything: the tiredness, the worry, the feeling I’m not doing enough. I try to hide it so my partner won’t worry, but it’s hard to stop once it starts.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t felt that. I’m exhausted and overwhelmed, but I haven’t thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like myself again and be a good mom.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression Screening Note  
Date: [today]  
Clinician: [name], LCSW  

Presenting symptoms endorsed (EPDS items paraphrased):  
- Marked anhedonia: minimal laughter/pleasure, anticipatory enjoyment absent  
- Pervasive low mood with crying spells, “heavy, gray feeling” daily  
- Excessive self-blame/guilt regarding infant care  
- Persistent, intrusive worry and physiologic panic episodes without clear trigger  
- Sleep disturbance secondary to ruminating and hyper-vigilance re: infant safety  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed/drowning in routine tasks  

Pattern: Consistent with moderate-to-severe depressive and anxiety symptoms postpartum.  
Safety: Denies self-harm or suicidal ideation (EPDS item 10 = 0).  
Risk factors: Primiparous, high self-expectations, limited reported support.  

Screening impression: High likelihood of major postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; recommend formal psychiatric evaluation and follow-up monitoring.
